correctness.rationale: Party-local orthogonal mode changes split off pure relative modes, reducing each replica determinant to at most three collective modes. For the tripartite determinant the top eigenspace of the rank-pattern matrix intersects its replica-shifted copy in exactly the one-dimensional vector fixed by both row and column replica cycles, so \(2N\) is a simple top eigenvalue; every other eigenvalue is strictly smaller. Consequently the determinant has exactly one vanishing factor as \(\lambda\to0\). The corresponding bipartite determinant has the analogous simple factor. The source-state parameter satisfies \(\lambda=(N-1)(N^2a^2)^{-1}+O(a^{-4})\), independently rederived symbolically here. Fresh numerical eigenspectrum checks for replica indices \(3,4,5\) and unequal block sizes confirmed top-eigenvalue multiplicity one. The frozen verifier was read and additionally matches published small exact cases.
correctness.risk: The proof is for integer replica index; analytic continuation in \(n\) is not claimed.

value.rationale: This proves an explicit conjecture posed by the source across every integer replica index and every nonempty tripartition, while identifying a concrete spectral reason for universality: a unique replica-constant top mode. The simple-nullity mechanism is structural and reusable beyond checking a finite table.
value.risk: The result does not address noninteger analytic continuation or nonsymmetric Gaussian states for \(n>2\).

final_claim: For every fully symmetric pure \(N\)-mode Gaussian state in the Camargo-Nishida family, every nonempty tripartition, and every integer replica index \(n\ge3\), the large-squeezing genuine tripartite multi-entropy has leading term \((2-n)(2n)^{-1}\log a\), with a finite positive determinant constant and error \(O(a^{-2})\).
limitations: Fully symmetric pure Gaussian family and nonempty tripartitions only.
